title: Unify helper text, affixes, and character-count behavior across form inputs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: There are multiple subtle inconsistencies in how helper text, prefix/suffix affixes (icons, units, tags), and character-counts behave across text fields, textareas, and select-like inputs. These inconsistencies lead to surprising truncation, poor screen-reader announcements, layout shifts, and duplicated visual treatments between desktop and mobile. Goal: define a single, accessible, and token-driven pattern for helper copy, affix semantics, and character-counts that works across the design system's input primitives and is implementable in the component library.
background: Observed problems: 1) Helper text sometimes collapses when error text appears; other times it persists below the error. 2) Prefix/suffix width is handled inconsistently — some inputs reserve space, others overlay content on small viewports. 3) Character-count placement differs between textarea and single-line inputs, causing layout jumps. 4) ARIA relationships are missing on several components (aria-describedby not consistently set), producing noisy or missing screen reader output. 5) Token usage for spacing/typography around affixes is ad-hoc; engineering ends up with many CSS overrides.
proposal: 1) Decide canonical rules: helper copy persists below the input and is a lower-priority visual style when there is an error; error text always replaces helper text for voiceover but both can be present visually with error taking precedence styling-wise. 2) Affixes: always allocate reserved space for prefix and suffix; define three size slots (compact, default, roomy) controlled by tokens; affixes should not overlap input text. 3) Character-count: consistent placement to the right of the helper row for single-line inputs and the bottom-right for textareas; counts should be visually muted and announce remaining/used counts to screen readers. 4) Accessibility: establish clear aria-describedby patterns linking input->helper/error->count (single id or comma-separated ids) and provide example snippets for React, vanilla HTML, and mobile. 5) Tokens: introduce spacing tokens (input-affix-gap, input-helper-gap), typography tokens for helper and count, and a token for affix reserved width variants.
acceptance_criteria:
- Updated component spec in Figma with examples for each input size and state (default / focused / error / disabled / with prefix / with suffix / with both / with char-count).
- Token list added to design tokens sheet and a migration note for engineering.
- Engineering story created that implements behavior with accessible markup and responsive behavior.
- Visual tests (Chromatic or Percy) capture helper + error + count combinations.
- Mobile screenshots for narrow widths show reserved affix spacing without overlap.
- Example code snippets for aria-describedby and screen-reader text included in the spec.
- UX review sign-off from PM and Eng and a rollout plan to migrate existing usages in Console routes over two sprints.
tasks: Update Figma components and tokens page
Write canonical spec doc with code examples
Coordinate with ENG to add CSS tokens and aria patterns
Audit top 10 Console pages for current anti-patterns
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Existing pages might rely on the old collapsing helper behavior which could change visual layout. Mitigation: migration flag + per-page review; provide a compatibility mixin for one release cycle. Risk: Screen reader behavior could change for some customers. Mitigation: test with NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver and include accessible examples and notes in the changelog.
notes: We discovered a related token gap while prototyping: input-affix-reserved-min should be added to avoid collapse when icons are swapped at runtime. Also recommend adding a utility CSS class for 'input--affix-compact' to ease migration.
